policy: One scoped task per autonomous PR. Each task declares one implementing agent role, objective and executable acceptance criteria. Tasks are complete only after merge and exact-head CI success; skipped agent runs or draft PRs do not count.

tasks.title: Add deterministic command history and replay
tasks.objective: Record typed player commands and ruleset version for each material state transition. Add replay from initial seed and command sequence. Do not duplicate state or reimplement gameplay rules in the API.
acceptance: A fixed seed and ordered command sequence reconstruct identical canonical GameState snapshots.
Invalid commands do not append events or mutate the saved state.
Tests cover replay of spins, nudge, absorption, battle and wave progression.

tasks.title: Extend the deterministic tactical auto-battle engine
tasks.objective: Extend the deterministic tactical auto-battle beyond the delivered role-based 3×3 formation and lane-aware targeting slice. Add player-editable positions, range/blocked-lane rules, typed armour and shields, cooldown-based class abilities, status effects, advanced boss targeting patterns and explicit turn-cap resolution. Keep every rule in pure Rust slotbound-core and expose causal events to the browser.
acceptance: Player formation changes validate a unique legal row/lane slot and persist; swaps are atomic and deterministic.
Range and blocked-lane rules define legal targets; if no target is reachable, the unit follows a documented wait/reposition rule.
Every ability has a documented cooldown/trigger condition and resource/state prerequisites.
Armour, shields, status application and expiry resolve in one documented order.
Boss telegraphs identify affected lane/targets before damage resolves.
Tests cover victory, defeat, simultaneous elimination, empty army, turn cap, status stacking and deterministic replay.
tasks.delivery_notes: The initial role-based 3×3 formation slice is implemented on feat/slotbound-tactical-combat: deterministic positions, lane-aware/front-row targeting, Guardian taunt precedence and target-specific boss telegraphs are covered by Rust tests and rendered from battle snapshots. Remaining scope is player-editable positions, range/blocked-lane rules, cooldown abilities, armour/shields/status order, boss targeting patterns and turn-cap coverage.

tasks.title: Create a versioned ruleset and balance simulator
tasks.objective: Move all economy, symbol distribution, progression and enemy scaling constants into a versioned typed ruleset. Add a seeded Monte Carlo simulator that reports win rate, run length, gold and summon distributions.
acceptance: No balance constant remains duplicated across API and browser presentation.
Same ruleset version and seed always produce the same result.
Simulator output includes sample count, seed range and uncertainty intervals.

tasks.title: Add a second sigil-board manipulation tool and modifier loadout
tasks.objective: Implement a limited-use Blast action with explicit cost and state validation, then model reel tools as typed modifiers rather than UI-only shortcuts.
acceptance: Blast cannot be used twice in one wave unless a defined modifier grants it.
Invalid target or phase leaves the board and resources unchanged.
Tests cover all modifier combinations and replay determinism.

tasks.title: Expand imprints and promotion branches
tasks.objective: Replace the single imprint string with a typed collection of imprint slots, donor inheritance rules and promotion tree nodes. Preserve stable unit identity and prevent self-feeding or locked-unit consumption.
acceptance: Imprint slot capacity and eligibility are validated in the domain.
Absorption is atomic and deterministic with a typed result preview.
Promotion choices are data-driven and covered at every threshold.

tasks.title: Add stage map, enemy roster and boss abilities
tasks.objective: Introduce versioned stages, enemy definitions, wave compositions and boss abilities. Keep enemy data original and separate from any third-party game's proprietary tables.
acceptance: A run selects and persists a stage and stage ruleset.
Boss encounter effects are deterministic and visible before combat.
Tests cover stage boundaries and boss reward conditions.

tasks.title: Add browser end-to-end player journey tests
tasks.objective: Add Playwright coverage against the real API for new run, spin, roster management, absorption, battle, item purchase, reload and run restoration. Do not replace real API calls with mocks in acceptance tests.
acceptance: The full first-wave journey passes in a real browser.
Reload restores the same saved run state.
Errors, disabled actions and small-screen layout receive coverage.

tasks.title: Build the original pixel-art asset and tile pipeline
tasks.objective: Replace code-only character placeholder drawing with a validated, versioned asset manifest and authored pixel-grid data. Add original animation strips and a Mosslight Meadow tile set; record provenance and keep all rendering strictly 2D with nearest-neighbour scaling.
acceptance: Every asset has a manifest entry with dimensions, palette role, provenance/licence, frame count and loop policy.
Common ally silhouettes are distinct at native 1x and integer-scaled 2x.
Tile edges/corners join without seams and biome props align to the 16x16 logical grid.
Asset validation rejects off-grid sizes, unknown palette keys, missing provenance and malformed frame strips.
Browser renderer reads the manifest and does not contain duplicated hard-coded asset palettes.

tasks.title: Animate automatic combat from authoritative event streams
tasks.objective: Create a legible 2D battle playback that consumes the authoritative Rust event stream, animates attacks, hit reactions, healing, defeats and boss telegraphs, and supports skip/reduced-motion controls without altering combat outcomes.
acceptance: Playback ordering and event counts exactly match the returned server event sequence.
Skip and reduced-motion render the same final state and event summary.
No client-side combat calculations or random outcomes are introduced.
Keyboard controls, focus management and mobile layout remain usable.

tasks.title: Version saves and add run ownership and recovery
tasks.objective: Add explicit save schema versions and safe migrations, idempotency for mutating API commands, run ownership/authentication and database backup/restore rehearsal without weakening transaction safety.
acceptance: Old save fixtures migrate to the current schema with unchanged gameplay state.
Repeated idempotency keys do not spend currency or advance RNG twice.
Unauthorised callers cannot read or mutate another player's run.
Migration and restore tests use a real ephemeral PostgreSQL instance.
Runtime database credentials cannot create or alter schema objects.

tasks.title: Add branching route map and biome progression
tasks.objective: Implement a deterministic authored route map with battle, rest, shop, event and boss nodes, then connect it to original biome/stage content. Keep route generation in the domain and visualisation in the browser.
acceptance: A fixed seed and ruleset version produce an identical route graph.
Every route has at least one reachable boss path and no unreachable mandatory node.
Node choices persist atomically and invalid moves leave route state unchanged.
Biome/stage transitions change encounters and visual tile set without changing past battle reports.

tasks.title: Expand and balance the seeded journey event director
tasks.objective: Build on the five implemented event families. Add biome and wave eligibility, event rarity weights in a versioned ruleset, repeat policies, delayed consequences, elite/hazard encounters and event-specific telemetry. Preserve deterministic generation and atomic choice resolution.
acceptance: Event weights and eligibility are versioned ruleset data rather than hard-coded UI values.
A fixed seed, ruleset version and command sequence reproduce the same event offers and outcomes.
Every event choice declares its costs, preconditions, state mutations, rewards and failure behavior.
Event history prevents duplicate rewards and supports save migration.
Monte Carlo reports event frequencies and choice outcomes across a documented seed range.
